nextClue.explanation: The trial proved the lower pressure is sustainable with no complaints. Making it permanent locks in the leakage and break benefit, while the verified meter needs no annual replacement.

clueText.nc-a: Six months at 420 kPa hold night flow near 6.5 L/s and breaks fall to one in the period.
clueText.nc-b: Returning to 480 kPa would restore the pressure driving both the leakage trend and the breaks.
clueText.nc-c: Meter accuracy was verified, so replacement does not address pressure driven losses.

tasks.prompt: Leak noise loggers in an Ontario DMA report a loud leak every night near a trunk main, but excavation at the loudest point finds a sound main.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional DMA crossed by a 600 mm trunk main feeding the next pressure zone. Loggers are on distribution hydrants. Night work only.

evidence.label: Leak noise peaks between 01:00 and 03:00 and is loudest on hydrants closest to the trunk main crossing.
Excavation at the correlation peak exposes the 200 mm distribution main in sound condition with no leak.
A partially open trunk main washout valve is found discharging to a chamber drain during the same night hours on a flushing timer.
When the washout timer is disabled for one night, logger noise across the DMA falls to background.
DMA inlet night flow does not change on the quiet night, staying at its normal 2.6 L/s.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The distribution leak moved away from the excavation before crews arrived
The noise source is the trunk washout discharging on a timer, transmitted through the network, not a distribution leak
The loggers are all faulty and produce false noise on a nightly schedule
A leak on the trunk main itself is losing DMA water at night

inference.explanation: Inlet flow never changed, so no DMA water was being lost. The noise follows the washout timer exactly and stops when it is disabled, and the excavated main is sound. Loggers correctly reported a real water noise.

nextClue.prompt: Which record check should precede future excavations on logger evidence alone?

options.label: Excavate a second point at the next loudest hydrant
Check trunk main appurtenance schedules, including washouts and air valves, against the noise hours before digging
Replace all leak loggers in the DMA with a different model

nextClue.explanation: Matching noise hours against scheduled discharges prevents digging on transmitted operational noise. The loggers performed correctly, so replacing them does not fix the interpretation error.

clueText.nc-a: A second dig would repeat the same error, since the source is a scheduled discharge, not a buried leak.
clueText.nc-b: The pre dig checklist is adopted, and the next two noise events are both matched to scheduled operations without excavation.
clueText.nc-c: Loggers accurately reported real flowing water noise, so the fault is in interpretation, not the instruments.

tasks.prompt: An Ontario DMA contains a hospital with steady night use. Its night flow jumps by 2.0 L/s one night and stays there, and the hospital insists its use is unchanged.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional DMA. The hospital is separately metered with hourly logging. DMA night flow baseline 5.5 L/s including hospital use of about 2.5 L/s.

evidence.label: DMA night flow rose from 5.5 L/s to 7.5 L/s on one night and held the new level for three weeks.
The hospital hourly meter record shows its night draw unchanged at 2.5 L/s plus or minus 0.1 L/s across the step.
No other large user in the DMA changed operations, and residential billed use is flat.
A step test isolates a 1.9 L/s drop to the section containing a 30 year old watermain along the hospital rear laneway.
Acoustic correlation on that section places leak noise 30 m from a hydrant, and the laneway asphalt shows a fresh shallow depression.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The hospital increased its night use but its meter failed to record the increase
The DMA inlet meter stepped up by 2.0 L/s due to an air slug
A new distribution leak on the laneway main accounts for the step, not a change in hospital use
Seasonal cooling tower use at the hospital explains the sustained step

inference.explanation: The hospital meter record directly contradicts a hospital increase, and its meter shows no step at all. The step test and correlation locate a matching 1.9 L/s loss on one section, with surface signs. An air slug cannot sustain a three week step.

nextClue.prompt: Which evidence should be shared with the hospital to close the dispute?

options.label: The annual system water audit summary
A photograph of the laneway depression alone
The paired hospital meter trend and DMA step test record showing its draw flat while the laneway section carries the step

nextClue.explanation: Paired records answer the claim directly: hospital draw flat, DMA step located elsewhere. A photo alone does not quantify flows, and the annual audit is too coarse for a one night step.

clueText.nc-a: The annual audit cannot resolve a single night step in one DMA.
clueText.nc-b: A depression can have many causes, so the photo alone does not prove where the 2.0 L/s is going.
clueText.nc-c: The hospital accepts the paired records, and repair of the laneway main returns DMA night flow to 5.6 L/s.

tasks.prompt: Two Ontario DMAs are separated by a normally closed boundary valve. After a trunk repair, both DMAs report distorted night flows in opposite directions.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional DMAs A and B. A trunk repair required opening the A to B boundary valve for supply support. Repair finished two weeks ago.

evidence.label: DMA A night flow fell from 5.0 L/s to 2.1 L/s after the repair, an apparent improvement with no leak repairs in A.
DMA B night flow rose from 3.0 L/s to 5.8 L/s in the same week, with no breaks or new users in B.
Combined A plus B night flow is 7.9 L/s, close to the 8.0 L/s combined figure before the repair.
The boundary valve log sheet for the repair was never closed out, and field check finds the valve still open.
Pressures in A and B, formerly 30 kPa apart, have equalised since the repair.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: DMA A fixed its leakage and DMA B developed a leak in the same week by coincidence
Both DMA inlet meters drifted in opposite directions during the repair
Customers moved consumption from DMA B to DMA A during the repair
The boundary valve was left open after the repair, so A now feeds part of B and both district balances are invalid

inference.explanation: Opposite moves of equal size, a constant combined total, and equalised pressures all point to water crossing the boundary. The valve is found open with its log sheet unclosed. Simultaneous opposite meter drifts and a coincidental leak pair do not fit the combined total.

nextClue.prompt: Which closeout control best prevents this distortion after future repairs?

options.label: Require boundary valve restoration and sign off as a hold point before the repair job can be closed
Recalculate both DMA allowances to match the new night flows
Average the two DMA night flows for reporting until they settle

nextClue.explanation: A hold point makes restoring district discreteness part of the repair itself. Recalculating allowances or averaging would institutionalise an invalid boundary.

clueText.nc-a: With the valve closed and signed off, A returns to 4.9 L/s and B to 3.1 L/s on the next night.
clueText.nc-b: New allowances would hide the open boundary and corrupt both leakage trends.
clueText.nc-c: Averaging hides which district holds any real loss and delays restoring the boundary.

tasks.prompt: An Ontario DMA supplied through a PRV shows night flow that tracks inlet pressure hour by hour, rising and falling with it each night.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional PRV fed DMA, average night pressure varying between 350 and 500 kPa as the upstream zone cycles. Legitimate night use is small and steady.

evidence.label: DMA night flow varies from 3.0 L/s at 350 kPa to 5.2 L/s at 500 kPa within single nights, following pressure with no time lag.
Customer night use in the DMA is dominated by a few steady process users whose metered draw is flat all night.
The same pressure flow relationship repeats every night for a month with no breaks reported.
A fixed outlet PRV trial holding 360 kPa for one week holds night flow near 3.1 L/s every night.
Acoustic surveys find widespread low level joint noise that gets louder as pressure rises.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Background leakage in this DMA is strongly pressure dependent, so pressure control, not point leak hunting, is the primary remedy
A large leak opens and closes in step with pressure each night
Customer process users vary their draw in step with pressure
The inlet flow meter reads high whenever pressure is high

inference.explanation: Metered process use is flat, so customers do not explain the swing. A single leak cycling nightly for a month with no break surfacing is implausible, while joint noise rising with pressure and the fixed pressure trial holding flow low both confirm pressure dependent background loss.

nextClue.prompt: Which PRV control mode best fits this DMA?

options.label: Fixed high outlet pressure to keep fire flow margins at all hours
Flow modulated or time based pressure control that holds the lowest adequate night pressure
Removing the PRV so the DMA follows upstream pressure

nextClue.explanation: Night pressure can be lowered when demand is lowest, cutting the pressure dependent loss. Removing control or fixing a high outlet preserves the loss the trial just measured.

clueText.nc-a: A fixed high outlet keeps night pressure near the top of the range that produced 5.2 L/s losses.
clueText.nc-b: Under modulated control, average night flow falls to 3.2 L/s with minimum service pressure maintained.
clueText.nc-c: Without the PRV the DMA would follow upstream swings up to 500 kPa, the worst condition measured.

tasks.prompt: An Ontario utility compares two similar DMAs. DMA One loses 8 L per service per hour at night. DMA Two loses 2 L per service per hour. Both have similar age mains.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional paired DMAs, each about 2,000 services, similar mains age and length. Pressures differ: DMA One averages 520 kPa, DMA Two averages 340 kPa.

evidence.label: Per service night loss is four times higher in DMA One than DMA Two, with similar mains condition scores.
DMA One average pressure is 520 kPa against 340 kPa in DMA Two, the largest pressure difference in the system.
Break records per 100 km are similar in the two DMAs over five years.
Soil type, service material, and customer profiles are closely matched between the DMAs.
A pressure reduction pilot in one subzone of DMA One cut its per service night loss by 40 percent.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: DMA One mains are in far worse condition than DMA Two mains
The loss difference is driven mainly by operating pressure, not by mains condition
DMA One customers waste far more water at night than DMA Two customers
DMA One has a single very large undetected leak

inference.explanation: Condition scores and break rates are matched, so condition does not explain a fourfold difference. A single leak would not respond across a whole subzone pilot, while the pilot cut losses 40 percent by pressure alone, matching the pressure gap between the districts.

nextClue.prompt: Which system wide lesson should the utility record?

options.label: Renew DMA One mains before any other district regardless of pressure
Raise DMA Two pressure to match DMA One for consistency
Set district pressure targets as a leakage control, since per service losses track pressure where condition is similar

nextClue.explanation: The paired comparison isolates pressure as the variable that differs and responds. Renewal may still be needed in time, but the evidence ranks pressure control first, and raising Two would raise its losses.

clueText.nc-a: Renewing first ignores the pilot result showing 40 percent loss reduction from pressure alone.
clueText.nc-b: Raising DMA Two pressure would be expected to raise its per service losses toward DMA One levels.
clueText.nc-c: District pressure targets are adopted, and DMA One is scheduled for PRV control before any renewal decision.

tasks.prompt: A step test in an Ontario DMA is planned for Tuesday night, but a watermain break in the next DMA on Monday forces a boundary change that nobody records.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional DMAs C and D. To support D during its break repair, a C to D boundary valve was opened Monday and left open. The C step test ran Tuesday as scheduled.

evidence.label: Tuesday step test results for DMA C are erratic: closing C sections sometimes raises inlet flow instead of lowering it.
DMA C pressure during the test is 25 kPa higher than its normal night pressure.
DMA D, under repair, shows supply holding up better than expected for a district on one feed.
The C to D boundary valve is found open on Wednesday, with no entry in the C test record.
Repeating the C step test the following week with the boundary confirmed closed gives clean, repeatable section drops.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: DMA C has several leaks that open and close randomly during tests
The Tuesday test crew operated the wrong valves throughout
The Tuesday test is invalid because DMA C was not discrete: the open boundary to D let flows shift during section closures
The inlet logger malfunctioned on Tuesday night only

inference.explanation: Higher than normal pressure, flow rising on closures, and D holding up all fit an open inter district feed. The valve is found open, and the repeat test with a confirmed boundary is clean, which a logger fault or random leaks would not produce so neatly.

nextClue.prompt: Which test protocol change follows from this case?

options.label: Require a same night boundary verification, signed by the test lead, before any step test data is accepted
Repeat every step test three times and average the results
Run step tests only during the day when crews are larger

nextClue.explanation: Boundary verification is the control that failed. Averaging invalid data does not make it valid, and daytime tests are distorted by customer demand.

clueText.nc-a: The protocol is adopted, and the next four step tests all carry signed boundary verifications with clean results.
clueText.nc-b: Averaging cannot correct data collected while the district was open to another DMA.
clueText.nc-c: Daytime demand swamps night flow signals, which is why step tests are night work.

tasks.prompt: An Ontario PRV station controls well all summer but loses control on the coldest nights, when downstream pressure climbs toward upstream pressure.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional PRV station in an unheated chamber. The pilot sensing line runs exposed along the chamber wall. A sister station with an insulated, heat traced sensing line serves the next zone. Setpoint is 360 kPa, upstream is 610 kPa.

evidence.label: Downstream pressure holds 360 kPa plus or minus 12 kPa from April to November.
On nights below minus 15 C, downstream pressure climbs over hours to 540 kPa and stays there until morning thaw.
The sister station, with its sensing line insulated and heat traced, holds setpoint through the same cold nights.
Inspection finds the sensing line uninsulated where it leaves the chamber, with ice confirmed in a drained test section after a cold night.
The main valve and pilot test perfectly in a warm workshop test the following week.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The PRV main valve wears out every winter and recovers every spring
Upstream pressure rises only on cold nights and overwhelms the valve
Downstream customers use no water on cold nights, causing the rise
Ice in the exposed pilot sensing line blinds the PRV on cold nights, so the valve drifts open toward upstream pressure

inference.explanation: Workshop tests clear the valve, and wear cannot heal each spring. The sister station on the same upstream supply holds setpoint, excluding an upstream cause, while ice is physically confirmed in the sensing line that tells the pilot what downstream pressure is.

nextClue.prompt: Which station program fix prevents the winter loss of control?

options.label: Replace the PRV main valve every autumn
Insulate and heat trace PRV sensing lines at unheated stations and add them to the fall cold weather checklist
Raise the setpoint in winter to match the higher pressures

nextClue.explanation: Protecting the sensing line preserves control in the conditions that disable it. Annual valve replacement discards a valve that tests perfectly, and raising the setpoint accepts the overpressure that damages the zone.

clueText.nc-a: The valve passed a full workshop test, so replacement does not address ice in its sensing line.
clueText.nc-b: With the sensing line insulated and traced, the station holds setpoint through the next cold snap at minus 22 C.
clueText.nc-c: A higher winter setpoint would keep the zone at the excessive pressures customers experienced.
